findings.title: traceID field dropped from 'Plugin Request Completed' log entries
findings.body: The previous logRequest implementation explicitly added a "traceID" field (via tracing.TraceIDFromContext) to the log params for the 'Plugin Request Completed' message. This PR removes that code (and the tracing import) entirely, and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware/instrumentContext function that replaces part of the old logic does not add traceID to the context either. As a result, the completed-request log line permanently loses the trace correlation ID, which is a real observability regression: operators will no longer be able to correlate these log lines with distributed traces using the traceID field they previously relied on.

findings.title: Logger middleware silently depends on being placed after ContextualLoggerMiddleware
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx) to retrieve pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname fields that are only populated if ContextualLoggerMiddleware ran earlier in the chain and called log.WithContextualAttributes. This creates an implicit ordering dependency between NewContextualLoggerMiddleware and NewLoggerMiddleware that is not enforced anywhere (no assertion, no doc comment on either struct). If someone reorders CreateMiddlewares in the future (e.g. moving the logger middleware up, or adding another middleware in between that forks/clears the context), the 'Plugin Request Completed' log lines would silently drop these fields with no compile-time or runtime warning, making a difficult-to-detect regression.

findings.title: Test function still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware after rename to MetricsMiddleware
findings.body: The file was renamed to metrics_middleware_test.go and the production type/constructors were renamed from InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware, but the test function name 'TestInstrumentationMiddleware' (line 21) was left unchanged. This is inconsistent with the stated goal of the PR ('Better naming and consistency') and will confuse anyone searching for tests related to MetricsMiddleware.

findings.title: No dedicated tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware/instrumentContext logic
findings.body: This PR extracts instrumentContext and introduces a new exported middleware, ContextualLoggerMiddleware, as a standalone component responsible for attaching plugin/request metadata (pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, uname) to the context for downstream consumers (including LoggerMiddleware, which now critically depends on it). No test file was added to verify this behavior (e.g. that the attributes end up in the context and are retrievable via FromContext, or that CollectMetrics/QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth correctly instrument the context while SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream do not). Given that LoggerMiddleware now relies entirely on this middleware for several previously-explicit log fields, the lack of coverage is a meaningful gap.

findings.title: Logger name still references 'instrumentation' after the rename
findings.body: NewLoggerMiddleware is now constructed with log.New("plugin.instrumentation") even though the PR's stated purpose is to rename InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware for clarity and the contextual logger has been split out into its own middleware. Leaving the logger name as 'plugin.instrumentation' is inconsistent with the renaming effort and will make log filtering/searching by this name misleading now that it specifically backs the request-completion logger rather than instrumentation/metrics.
